name: Willis Towers Watson
legalName: Willis Towers Watson Public Limited Company

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (File:Logo WTW.png, 1920x1080 current lowercase purple mark; the en.wikipedia infobox PNG is only 146x67)

description: WTW is an Irish-incorporated, London-based advisory and insurance broking firm. It earns fees and commissions in two halves: about 55 percent of segment revenue comes from advising and administering employee benefits, pensions, investments and pay for employers (Health, Wealth & Career), and about 45 percent from brokering commercial insurance and selling insurance-industry consulting and software (Risk & Broking). It bears no insurance risk itself; clients pay consulting fees, and insurers pay commissions on policies placed. Consulting revenue is steady and seasonal (benefits and pay cycles in the second half); brokerage follows premium rates and client exposure. It sold its TRANZACT Medicare-enrolment business on 2024-12-31, which is why 2025 reported revenue fell while organic revenue grew 5 percent.

employees.note: Approximately 47,000 colleagues serving more than 140 countries and markets: Health, Wealth & Career 23,100 and Risk & Broking 16,800 by segment (remainder corporate).

businessLines.name: Health, Wealth & Career (HWC)
businessLines.how: Employers pay consulting and administration fees for benefits advice and brokerage, pension and retirement actuarial work, discretionary investment management (asset-based fees), pay and career consulting, and outsourced benefits administration; insurers also pay commissions on benefits placed. Mostly recurring annual engagements, with a seasonal second half.

businessLines.name: Risk & Broking (R&B)
businessLines.how: Commissions from insurers (a share of premium) or negotiated fees from clients for placing commercial insurance (Corporate Risk & Broking places more than $34 billion of premium a year), plus fees and software licences from insurers for insurance consulting and technology.
